claims.text: The investigated material is an additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy containing a nanoscale dispersion of dual nanoprecipitates.
Integrating atom probe tomography with in situ high-temperature TEM/EDS can elucidate nanoscale elemental redistribution during oxidation.
During high-temperature oxidation, nanoprecipitates undergo directional elemental redistribution.
Al, Cr, or Ti becomes enriched at specific interfaces during oxidation.
Redistribution of Al, Cr, or Ti promotes locally protective oxide phases.
Nanoprecipitate-driven protective oxide formation enhances oxidation resistance relative to cast and wrought variants.
The alloy is to be oxidized at 900–1100 °C under controlled oxygen partial pressure.
The proposed temperature range is analogous to high-temperature service in gas-turbine or aerospace applications.
Nanoprecipitates act as loci for elemental segregation during oxidation.
Nanoprecipitates act as loci for phase transformation during oxidation.
Al, Cr, and Ti migrate from nanoprecipitates toward the oxide interface under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Migration of Al, Cr, and Ti enables formation of a dense protective oxide scale.
Selective elemental redistribution mediates oxidation kinetics and improves high-temperature performance.
The emerging oxide-scale composition will be spatially correlated with nanoprecipitate chemistry.
Protective elements will be directionally enriched at the oxide interface relative to the bulk matrix.
Directional redistribution will be absent or less pronounced in cast and wrought counterparts.
Cast and wrought versions lack the distinctive nanostructuring produced by additive manufacturing.
Oxidation and redistribution behavior may change under different temperatures or oxygen environments.
APT can generate three-dimensional elemental maps of nanoprecipitates and surrounding oxidized regions.
Failure to observe significant directional redistribution or a correlation between oxide and nanoprecipitate chemistry would falsify the proposed redistribution mechanism.

contradictions.description: The intervention suggests that integrated APT and in situ TEM/EDS are performed during oxidation to capture real-time redistribution, whereas the experiment specifies time-resolved in situ TEM/EDS but only periodic ex situ APT.
